message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the long‑weekend holidays in Canada for 2023 (i.e., public holidays that fall on a Friday or Monday, giving you a three‑day weekend).  
(If you need the full list of all public holidays—including those that fall mid‑week—just let me know!)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend? |
|---------|-------------|-------------|---------------|
| **New Year’s Day** | Jan 1 | Sunday | No (but you’ll still get a 4‑day break if you take the preceding Friday off) |
| **Family Day** (Alberta, Saskatchewan, New Brunswick, Ontario) | Feb 20 | Monday | Yes |
| **Good Friday** | Apr 7 | Friday | Yes |
| **Victoria Day** | May 22 | Monday | Yes |
| **Canada Day** | Jul 1 | Saturday | No (but you’ll get a 4‑day break if you take the preceding Friday off) |
| **Labour Day** | Sep 4 | Monday | Yes |
| **Thanksgiving** | Oct 9 | Monday | Yes |
| **Remembrance Day** | Nov 11 | Monday | Yes |
| **Christmas Day** | Dec 25 | Monday | Yes |
| **Boxing Day** | Dec 26 | Tuesday | No |

### Quick Takeaway
- **Long‑weekends** in 2023: Family Day (Feb 20), Good Friday (Apr 7), Victoria Day (May 22), Labour Day (Sep 4), Thanksgiving (Oct 9), Remembrance Day (Nov 11), Christmas Day (Dec 25).
- If you’re looking to plan a getaway around a holiday that falls mid‑week, you can still create a long weekend by taking a day off on either side (e.g., take Friday the 1st off for New Year’s Day, or take Monday the 27th off for Boxing Day).

Feel free to copy/paste this into your holiday‑planning app or let me know if you’d like it in a different format (JSON, CSV, etc.).
